Assertion (A): The line (−3 − x)/5 = (y − 5)/2 = (z + 4)/−5 has direction ratios 5, 2, −5.
Reason (R): In the standard form, x, y, z must have coefficient +1 in the numerators.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) Rewrite as (x + 3)/(−5): DRs are −5, 2, −5; A false, R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Show that the lines (x − 4)/−2 = (y + 2) = (z − 1)/3 and (x − 9)/−3 = (y + 6)/3 = (z − 1)/−3 intersect, by finding the shortest distance between them. Also find the point of intersection.
items.markingKey: (a⃗₂ − a⃗₁)·(b⃗₁ × b⃗₂) = 0 (3 marks); equate general points to find λ, μ (2 marks).

items.stem: Show that the lines (x − 1)/5 = (y + 3)/4 = (z − 2)/−3 and x/−10 = (y + 3)/−8 = (z + 2)/6 are parallel.
Find the distance between the parallel lines r⃗ = (−2î + ĵ − 2k̂) + λ(î − 2ĵ + 2k̂) and r⃗ = (−4î − 2ĵ + k̂) + μ(î − 2ĵ + 2k̂).
The vector equation of the line through the point with position vector a⃗ and parallel to b⃗ is …
options: r⃗ = b⃗ + λa⃗
r⃗ = a⃗ + λb⃗

items.stem: Priya stretches a zip-line from P(0, 2, 4) to Q(2, 8, 1) (metres) for a school camp. (i) Find the direction ratios of PQ. (ii) Find the length PQ. (iii) Find the direction cosines of PQ.
Find the value of k so that the lines (x + 2) = (y − 4)/−5 = (z − 4)/−3 and x/−5 = y/k = (z + 3)/−5 are perpendicular to each other.
A line makes angles 90°, 60° and 30° with the positive x-, y- and z-axes. Find its direction cosines.
items.markingKey: l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ; check l² + m² + n² = 1.
